doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bandleaders and the audience: Tommy Dorsey, Goodman and Shaw
summary: Tommy liked success, Shaw saw the audience as a necessary evil, and his lectures are titled 'Three Chords for Beauty and One to Pay the Rent.'

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Thinking about the bandleader and the audience aspect . . .
. . . how do you think your contemporaries at the time, like, say, Tommy Dorsey or Benny Goodman, people like that, how did they . . . did they handle it differently from you?

I don’t know. I can’t say. I know that Tommy liked the audience. He liked success. I thought the audience was a necessary evil. They paid the freight. You needed them. My lectures are called “Three Chords for Beauty and One to Pay the Rent.” One for the rent is o.k. So I would play Beguine if they wanted. I didn’t want to play it anymore.
